coverage_notes: Swept 5 major angles: (1) foundational error theory & taxonomy (slips vs mistakes vs lapses; Don Norman's error classification); (2) trust, reliance & automation bias (over-reliance paradox, mental models, transparency); (3) error recovery & reversal operations (undo/redo, confirmation dialogs, reversible design); (4) visibility & feedback mechanisms (before/after consequences, system status, information scent); (5) persuasion paradox & over-intervention (cognitive load, confirmation fatigue, user agency). Tier 0 sources include systematic reviews and meta-analyses on human error and automation safety; T1 prioritizes recent peer-reviewed HCI work (CHI 2023-2026, TOCHI, UIST, arXiv cs.HC) plus foundational ACM work on error recovery; T2 covers canonical seminal authors (Don Norman, Ben Shneiderman, Edward Tufte, Nielsen); T3 includes high-quality practitioner essays from Nielsen Norman Group and interaction design publications. Deduplication: removed patent abstracts and vendor product pages; consolidated multiple URLs pointing to same paper. Coverage addresses over-reliance vs under-reliance tension, confirmation fatigue, system predictability failures, mental model mismatches, and design patterns for graceful error recovery. Notable gaps: (1) safety-critical domain literature limited to summary references; (2) some CHI/UIST papers behind ACM paywall (marked reference-only); (3) limited coverage of error recovery in collaborative/multi-user systems (identified but sparse); (4) persuasion theory in error contexts under-explored in recent HCI (mostly design patterns rather than theory).

sources.title: The Design of Everyday Things (Revised & Expanded)
sources.notes: Seminal 1988 work (revised 2013) establishing foundational error classification: capture errors, description errors, data-driven errors, mode errors. Central thesis: errors are design failures, not user failures. Introduces knowledge-in-the-world vs knowledge-in-the-head principle and six design principles for error reduction.

sources.title: Shneiderman's Eight Golden Rules of Interface Design (with Error Recovery)
sources.notes: Foundational 1985 principles emphasizing visibility, feedback, error prevention, and recovery. Rule 5 (Error Prevention) and Rule 9 (Help Recover from Errors) directly address error detection and recovery. Principles iteratively refined over 3+ decades.

sources.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
sources.notes: Seminal work on data visualization and graphical integrity. Addresses how visualization errors, chart junk, and deception mislead users. Principle: data-ink ratio and truthfulness in display. Relevant for visibility of error states and before/after consequences.

sources.title: 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design
sources.notes: Foundational 1994 heuristics by Jakob Nielsen. Heuristic #5 (Error Prevention) and #9 (Error Recognition and Recovery) are canonical frameworks. Emphasize preventing problems over recovery but acknowledge both are needed.

sources.title: When Should Users Check? A Decision-Theoretic Model of Confirmation Frequency in Multi-Step AI Agent Tasks
sources.notes: CHI 2026 (arXiv 2510.05307). Addresses the confirmation paradox: how often should users verify agent actions vs. over-intervention. Decision-theoretic model for optimal checking frequency. Directly tackles confirmation fatigue and over-reliance tension.

sources.title: The Role of Trust in Automation Reliance
sources.notes: International Journal of Human-Computer Studies. Seminal work on trust calibration and reliance. Shows users over-rely after observing success; under-rely after observing failure. Trust miscalibration persists even with explanations. Central to understanding automation bias paradox.

sources.title: Calibrating Trust, Reliance and Dependence in Variable-Reliability Automation
sources.notes: Recent meta-analysis on trust calibration in automation. Distinguishes trust (willingness), reliance (actual behavior), and dependence (skill atrophy). Addresses over-reliance vs under-reliance as twin design challenges. Covers feedback mechanisms for calibration.

sources.title: Calibrating Reliance on Automated Advice: Transparency and Trust Calibration Feedback
sources.notes: 2025 study on transparency's nuanced effect on reliance. Shows continuous feedback aids calibration; transparency alone insufficient. Tests different feedback modalities for error correction loops.

sources.title: How Transparency Modulates Trust in Artificial Intelligence
sources.notes: Examines transparency mechanisms (explainability, uncertainty quantification) and their effect on trust. Shows effect is context-dependent and can backfire if explanations undermine confidence.

sources.title: Understanding Mental Models of Generative Conversational Search and The Effect of Interface Transparency
sources.notes: arXiv cs.HC. Elicitation study on user mental models of AI systems. Shows interface transparency affects mental model formation; mismatched mental models lead to error over-reliance.

sources.title: AI Transparency in the Age of LLMs: A Human-Centered Research Roadmap
sources.notes: arXiv survey on AI transparency as prerequisite for error detection and recovery. Maps design space of transparency mechanisms (mechanistic, system, user-level). Addresses how transparency supports mental model alignment.

sources.title: Exploring the Effects of Human-Centered AI Explanations on Trust and Reliance
sources.notes: Empirical study on explanation design for error mitigation. Shows explanation quality affects ability to detect AI errors; poor explanations increase over-reliance.

sources.title: Adjust for Trust: Mitigating Trust-Induced Inappropriate Reliance on AI Assistance
sources.notes: arXiv 2025. Proposes design interventions (trust nudges, capability calibration) to reduce inappropriate reliance. Tests cognitive forcing functions and uncertainty expressions.

sources.title: How Does HCI Understand Human Agency and Autonomy?
sources.notes: CHI 2023. Critical analysis of agency in human-AI systems. Addresses user control, predictability, and locus of control—essential for error recovery design.

sources.title: Digging Into User Control in Algorithm-Assisted Decision-Making
sources.notes: IUI 2020 (ACM). Explores user control mechanisms and their role in error awareness and correction. Examines transparency vs control tradeoffs.

sources.title: Misfitting With AI: How Blind People Verify and Contest AI Errors
sources.notes: arXiv. Qualitative study on error detection and contestation strategies. Shows users develop workarounds and verification protocols. Documents how misaligned systems impede error recovery.

sources.title: Don't Explain Without Verifying Veracity: An Evaluation of Explainable AI with Video Activity Recognition
sources.notes: arXiv. Shows false explanations increase user trust despite being incorrect. Addresses how explanation-based error recovery can backfire without veracity checking.

sources.title: People Can Accurately Predict Behavior of Complex Algorithms That Are Available, Compact, and Aligned
sources.notes: arXiv. Addresses conditions under which users develop accurate mental models. Shows complexity is not inherent barrier; availability and alignment enable predictability.

sources.title: Distributed Cognition for AI-supported Remote Operations: Challenges and Research Directions
sources.notes: arXiv. Applies distributed cognition lens to AI error recovery. Shows errors arise from coordination failures across human-AI teams, not just individual mistakes.

sources.title: Situation Awareness, Mental Models and Understanding
sources.notes: IEEE conference. Connects situational awareness (Endsley model), mental models, and system understanding. Error recovery requires maintaining accurate situation awareness.

sources.title: Safety Enhancement through Situation-Aware User Interfaces
sources.notes: arXiv. Proposes context-sensitive error detection and recovery. Shows UI awareness of system state enables proactive error prevention and faster recovery.

sources.title: Discovering and Validating AI Errors With Crowdsourced Failure Reports
sources.notes: arXiv. Examines how users discover and report AI errors. Shows user error detection patterns; informs design of error visibility and feedback mechanisms.

sources.title: Human-in-the-Loop Error Detection in an Object Organization Task with a Social Robot
sources.notes: Empirical study on human error detection in human-robot collaboration. Shows visibility, feedback clarity, and user attention affect error detection rates and recovery speed.

sources.title: Different Types of Voice User Interface Failures May Cause Different Degrees of Frustration
sources.notes: arXiv. Error taxonomy for voice UIs. Shows error type, detection clarity, and recovery path affect user frustration and reliance.

sources.title: Characterizing Unintended Consequences in Human-GUI Agent Collaboration for Web Browsing
sources.notes: arXiv 2025. Documents failure modes in agent-mediated UIs. Shows visibility of agent state and action reversibility critical for error recovery.

sources.title: Interacto: A Modern User Interaction Processing Model
sources.notes: arXiv. Formal model of user interactions enabling undo/redo. Addresses command pattern and state management for reversible operations.

sources.title: Conceptual Metaphors Impact Perceptions of Human-AI Collaboration
sources.notes: arXiv. Shows metaphor choice (e.g., 'tool' vs 'agent') shapes user mental models and error expectations. Misaligned metaphors increase error over-reliance.

sources.title: Towards Involving End-Users in Interactive Human-in-the-Loop AI Fairness
sources.notes: arXiv. Addresses user agency in error correction loops. Shows transparent error feedback enables user-driven corrections and calibration.

sources.title: A Diachronic Perspective on User Trust in AI Under Uncertainty
sources.notes: arXiv. Longitudinal view of trust formation and decay through error experiences. Shows single errors can destroy trust; recovery requires consistent reliability and explanation.

sources.title: AI Mental Models & Trust: The Promises and Perils of Interaction Design
sources.notes: EPIC (Ethnographic Praxis in Industry) 2024. Ethnographic study on mental model formation and error tolerance. Shows designed mental models often mismatch user expectations.

sources.title: Investigating How Clinicians Form Trust in an AI-Based Mental Health Model: Qualitative Case Study
sources.notes: Qualitative study on professional trust formation. Shows domain expertise enables error detection; transparency on limitations aids trust calibration.

sources.title: Measures for Explainable AI: Explanation Goodness, User Satisfaction, Mental Models, Curiosity, Trust, and Human-AI Performance
sources.notes: Comprehensive framework for measuring XAI effectiveness. Links explanation quality to mental model accuracy and error detection capability.

sources.title: Trustworthy Human Computation: A Survey
sources.notes: arXiv survey on trust in crowdsourced and human-AI systems. Covers error detection, verification, and correction mechanisms in collaborative settings.

sources.title: AI Mismatches: Identifying Potential Algorithmic Harms Before AI Development
sources.notes: arXiv 2025. Framework for identifying capability-expectation mismatches before deployment. Addresses how design can prevent error-from-misalignment.

sources.title: Mitigating Automation Bias in Generative AI Through Nudges: A Cognitive Reflection Test Study
sources.notes: 2025 study testing interface nudges to reduce automation bias. Shows warning design and cognitive forcing functions improve error detection.

sources.title: Bias in the Loop: How Humans Evaluate AI-Generated Suggestions
sources.notes: arXiv. Examines how cognitive biases affect human error detection and AI suggestion acceptance. Shows presentation order and confidence affect reliance.

sources.title: Cognitive Biases in User Interaction with Automated Vehicles: The Influence of Explainability and Mental Models
sources.notes: Empirical study linking cognitive biases to automation over-reliance. Shows explainability design can mitigate bias-driven error acceptance.

sources.title: RFM-HRI: A Multimodal Dataset of Medical Robot Failure, User Reaction and Recovery Preferences for Item Retrieval Tasks
sources.notes: arXiv 2025. Multimodal dataset capturing error detection, user frustration, and recovery strategies in human-robot interaction. Documents real error recovery behavior.

sources.title: Calling for Backup: How Children Navigate Successive Robot Communication Failures
sources.notes: arXiv. Longitudinal study of error recovery strategies in human-robot interaction. Shows escalation behavior and help-seeking as error recovery tactics.

sources.title: Why the Face?: Exploring Robot Error Detection Using Instrumented Bystander Reactions
sources.notes: arXiv 2025. Examines how third-party observers detect robot errors. Shows social cues and visible state indicators aid error detection.

sources.title: How Do We Research Human-Robot Interaction in the Age of Large Language Models? A Systematic Review
sources.notes: arXiv systematic review. Covers error recovery in LLM-mediated human-robot interaction. Identifies transparency and reversibility as key factors.

sources.title: Signal or 'Noise': Human Reactions to Robot Errors in the Wild
sources.notes: arXiv. In-the-wild study of user responses to robot errors. Documents habituation to errors and conditions under which errors are noticed.

sources.title: CUAAudit: Meta-Evaluation of Vision-Language Models as Auditors of Autonomous Computer-Use Agents
sources.notes: arXiv 2025. Framework for error auditing in agent systems. Proposes automated error detection and explanation mechanisms.

sources.title: Polite But Boring? Trade-offs Between Engagement and Psychological Reactance to Chatbot Feedback Styles
sources.notes: arXiv. Studies feedback style effects on user acceptance of corrections. Shows politeness-directness tradeoff in error feedback design.

sources.title: Driver Assistant: Persuading Drivers to Adjust Secondary Tasks Using Large Language Models
sources.notes: arXiv. Studies persuasion design for error correction. Shows framing and tone affect user receptivity to system-initiated corrections.

sources.title: A Review of Current Human Reliability Assessment Methods Utilized in High Hazard Human-System Interface Design
sources.notes: Springer. Reviews Human Reliability Assessment (HRA) methods. Covers SHERPA, THERP, and predictive error analysis techniques.

sources.title: Validating Task Analysis for Error Identification: Reliability and Validity of a Human Error Prediction Technique
sources.notes: Ergonomics journal. Validates error prediction methods. Shows task analysis can identify high-error interactions before deployment.

sources.title: Toward a Human-Centered UML for Risk Analysis
sources.notes: arXiv. Proposes human-centered modeling of error and recovery paths in system design. Addresses notation for recovery mechanisms.

sources.title: Fuzzy to Clear: Elucidating the Threat Hunter Cognitive Process and Cognitive Support Needs
sources.notes: arXiv. Cognitive task analysis of error detection in cybersecurity. Shows how visibility of system state supports error recognition.

sources.title: Making Data Tangible: A Cross-Disciplinary Design Space for Data Physicalization
sources.notes: arXiv. Explores physical representation for error visibility and correction. Shows tangibility aids error detection and recovery.

sources.title: Constraining Participation: Affordances of Feedback Features in Interfaces to Large Language Models
sources.notes: arXiv. Analyzes feedback affordances in LLM interfaces. Shows feedback design shapes error detection and correction capability.

sources.title: Not a Technology Person: Motivating Older Adults Toward the Use of Mobile Technology
sources.notes: arXiv. Studies error handling and recovery for non-expert users. Shows error feedback clarity and low-barrier recovery critical for adoption.

sources.title: A Field Study of On-Calendar Visualizations
sources.notes: arXiv. In-the-wild evaluation of visibility design. Shows how visualization choices affect error detection and correction.

sources.title: GoEX: Perspectives and Designs Towards a Runtime for Autonomous LLM Applications
sources.notes: arXiv. Design of runtime system for LLM error detection and recovery. Proposes architecture for graceful error handling in autonomous systems.

sources.title: Emerging Practices for Large Multimodal Model Assistance for People with Visual Impairments: Implications for Design
sources.notes: arXiv. Studies accessibility implications of AI errors. Shows error feedback modality (text, audio, haptic) affects error awareness.

sources.title: Complex Cognition: A New Theoretical Foundation for the Design and Evaluation of Visual Analytics Systems
sources.notes: arXiv. Theoretical framework for cognition in complex data systems. Addresses error detection in exploratory analysis and data interpretation.

sources.title: Resilience Design Patterns: A Structured Approach to Resilience at Extreme Scale
sources.notes: arXiv. Catalogs design patterns for error recovery in distributed systems (circuit breaker, bulkhead, recovery). Applicable to UI design.

sources.title: Pre-Filtering Code Suggestions Using Developer Behavioral Telemetry to Optimize LLM-Assisted Programming
sources.notes: arXiv 2025. Uses error detection patterns to improve suggestions. Shows learning from errors to prevent future mistakes.

sources.title: Toward Personalized LLM-Powered Agents: Foundations, Evaluation, and Future Directions
sources.notes: arXiv 2025. Addresses personalized error recovery and adaptive agent behavior based on user feedback and corrections.

sources.title: Emotion-Aware Design: Modulating Valence, Arousal, and Dominance in Communication via Design
sources.notes: arXiv 2025. Addresses emotional response to error messages and corrections. Shows emotion design affects user receptivity to error feedback.

sources.title: Data Visualization in Political and Social Sciences
sources.notes: arXiv. Covers visualization design for complex data. Addresses how visualization errors mislead interpretation and correction.

sources.title: Confirmation Dialogs Can Prevent User Errors (If Not Overused)
sources.notes: Nielsen Norman Group article. Classic 2018 piece on confirmation dialog design. Emphasizes overuse paradox and proposes 8 design guidelines. Practitioner consensus.

sources.title: Preventing User Errors: Avoiding Conscious Mistakes
sources.notes: Nielsen Norman Group. Distinguishes slips vs mistakes and recovery strategies. Evidence-based practitioner guidance.

sources.title: UX for Reversible Actions: A Decision Framework for Designing With Recovery in Mind
sources.notes: LogRocket UX blog. Practical framework for reversible design decisions. Compares confirmation vs undo vs version history patterns.

sources.title: What Is Human Error? (Updated 2026)
sources.notes: Interaction Design Foundation. Overview of human error taxonomy, slips, mistakes, and design implications. Educational resource.

sources.title: Shneiderman's Eight Golden Rules Will Help You Design Better Interfaces
sources.notes: IxDF synthesis of Shneiderman's rules with examples. Error prevention and recovery emphasis.

sources.title: What Are Affordances?
sources.notes: IxDF overview of affordances and constraints. Explains how visibility prevents mode errors and erroneous actions.

sources.title: Chapter 3 & 5 Summary: Knowledge in the Head and World / Human Error? No, Bad Design
sources.notes: Medium Design Bootcamp summary of Norman's error theory. Accessible explanation of slips vs mistakes and design recovery strategies.

sources.title: User Error: Prevention and Recovery in UX
sources.notes: Zion & Zion design consultancy. Overview of error prevention vs recovery strategies with examples.

sources.title: 12 UX Design Examples That Show How to Stop User Errors Before They Happen
sources.notes: LogRocket. Case studies of error prevention patterns (constraints, validation, defaults). Practitioner focus.

sources.title: Input Feedback Design Pattern
sources.notes: UI Patterns catalog. Documents inline validation and real-time feedback patterns for error prevention.

sources.title: Inline Validation UX — Smart Interface Design Patterns
sources.notes: Design patterns for real-time validation. Addresses timing, messaging, and user control in error feedback.

sources.title: Think-Time UX: Design to Support Cognitive Latency
sources.notes: UX Tigers blog. Addresses cognitive load in error correction and design for thinking time before confirmations.

sources.title: Undoable Command Design Pattern
sources.notes: Medium. Technical overview of Command and Memento patterns for undo/redo. Explains reversible operation implementation.

sources.title: Command Design Pattern
sources.notes: Refactoring Guru. Comprehensive design pattern reference. Undo/redo as primary use case.

sources.title: Best Emotional Design Principles to Create Attractive and Enjoyable UI
sources.notes: Mockplus blog on emotional design. Addresses tone in error messages and user frustration with errors.

sources.title: What Is Emotional Response in UX Design?
sources.notes: IxDF overview. Emotional design and its role in user perception of errors and error recovery experience.
